title: Procure-to-Pay
subtitle: From purchase request to supplier payment, documented as a functional analysis
thesis: One approved request. One traceable order. One payment that can be checked.
role: Process analysis, business rules, functional requirements, acceptance criteria
status: Analysis document only, no ERP configured, no supplier engaged
typeLabel: Independent learning case study, fictional scenario
boundary: Northline Industrial Supply is a fictional company created for this exercise. The process, rules and requirements are designed to demonstrate analysis, not to describe a real client. No ERP product was configured, no supplier was contacted, and no business outcome is claimed.

context.company: Northline Industrial Supply (fictional), a 120-person distributor of maintenance and repair supplies.
context.situation: Purchasing grew out of email and spreadsheets. Requests arrive by chat, email and paper. Managers approve by replying “OK”. Procurement raises orders in a spreadsheet, and the warehouse records receipts on a clipboard.
context.problem: The same purchase can exist in three versions: what was asked for, what was ordered, and what arrived. Finance reconciles them by hand before paying, so the payment is only as reliable as the folder it came from.
context.why: A structured procure-to-pay process makes the commitment traceable from request to payment. It also gives each actor one place to see what they own.

stakeholders.responsibility: Raises a purchase request with a business reason, quantity and required date.
stakeholders.interaction: Creates and tracks the request, and answers questions from procurement.

stakeholders.responsibility: Approves or rejects requests within an authority limit.
stakeholders.interaction: Reviews the request; a rejection returns it to the requester with a reason.

stakeholders.responsibility: Turns approved requests into purchase orders and selects the supplier.
stakeholders.interaction: Cannot order without an approved request; maintains supplier and item master data.

stakeholders.responsibility: Records what actually arrived against the order.
stakeholders.interaction: Creates a goods receipt that references a valid purchase order.

stakeholders.responsibility: Verifies the invoice against the order and receipt, then schedules payment.
stakeholders.interaction: Holds payment when quantities or prices do not match, and records why.

stakeholders.responsibility: Delivers goods and issues an invoice.
stakeholders.interaction: Outside the system boundary; receives the order and sends the invoice.

steps.name: Purchase request
steps.output: Request with items, quantity, reason and required date.

steps.name: Approval
steps.output: Approved or rejected request, with a reason.

steps.name: Purchase order
steps.output: Order linked to one approved request and one supplier.

steps.name: Goods receipt
steps.output: Receipt linked to the order, with accepted and rejected quantities.

steps.name: Invoice verification
steps.output: Matched invoice, or a documented exception.

steps.name: Payment
steps.output: Payment scheduled and an audit entry written.

exceptions: A rejected request returns to the requester; no order can be created.
A receipt with a different quantity creates a partial receipt and keeps the difference open.
An invoice that does not match is held, not paid, until the mismatch is resolved.

rules.rule: A purchase request must include at least one item, a quantity, a business reason and a required date before it can be submitted.
Only a department manager with an active approval role may approve or reject a request.
A request above the manager's authority limit requires the next approver in the hierarchy.
A purchase order can only be created from a request whose status is Approved.
A purchase order must reference exactly one approved request and one supplier.
A goods receipt must reference a valid, open purchase order.
Invoice verification compares ordered, received and invoiced quantity and price; any difference holds payment.
Payment can only be scheduled when the request is approved, the order exists, the receipt is recorded and the invoice is verified.
Every state change writes an audit entry with actor, timestamp and previous state.

requirements.title: Submit a purchase request
requirements.description: The system shall let a requester create a request with one or more items, quantity, business reason and required date.
requirements.behavior: An incomplete request cannot be submitted; missing fields are named.

requirements.title: Validate request data
requirements.description: The system shall validate required fields and reject a quantity of zero or less.
requirements.behavior: Validation messages appear next to the field and the request stays in Draft.

requirements.title: Approval queue
requirements.description: The system shall show each approver the requests waiting for their decision.
requirements.behavior: The queue shows requester, amount, reason and submitted date, oldest first.

requirements.title: Authority limit routing
requirements.description: The system shall route a request above the approver's limit to the next approver.
requirements.behavior: The request stays Pending and the next approver is notified.

requirements.title: Reject with a reason
requirements.description: The system shall require a reason when a request is rejected.
requirements.behavior: The request becomes Rejected and returns to the requester with the reason attached.

requirements.title: Create an order from an approved request
requirements.description: The system shall allow a purchase order to be created only from an approved request.
requirements.behavior: An unapproved request cannot be selected as the order source.

requirements.title: Link order to request and supplier
requirements.description: The system shall record one approved request and one supplier on each purchase order.
requirements.behavior: The order shows its source request and the agreed supplier price.

requirements.title: Goods receipt against an open order
requirements.description: The system shall let receiving record a receipt against a valid, open purchase order.
requirements.behavior: A receipt cannot be saved without an open order reference.

requirements.title: Partial receipt
requirements.description: The system shall record accepted and rejected quantities separately when the delivery differs from the order.
requirements.behavior: The order stays Partially received until the open quantity is resolved.

requirements.title: Three-way match
requirements.description: The system shall compare ordered, received and invoiced quantity and price before payment.
requirements.behavior: A difference moves the invoice to Held, with the mismatched field named.

requirements.title: Audit trail
requirements.description: The system shall write an audit entry for every state change.
requirements.behavior: Each entry records actor, timestamp and the previous state.

requirements.title: Role-based visibility
requirements.description: The system shall show each actor only the records their role owns.
requirements.behavior: A requester cannot open another department's requests.

acceptance.when: They submit a request with items, quantity, reason and required date
acceptance.then: The request is saved with status Submitted

acceptance.when: The requester submits without a business reason
acceptance.then: Submission is blocked and the missing field is named

acceptance.given: A request is Submitted and within the manager's limit
acceptance.then: The status becomes Approved and the audit entry is written

acceptance.given: A request is above the manager's limit
acceptance.then: The request stays Pending and moves to the next approver

acceptance.when: The manager rejects it with a reason
acceptance.then: The status becomes Rejected and no order can be created

acceptance.given: A request is Draft or Rejected
acceptance.when: Procurement tries to create an order
acceptance.then: The request cannot be selected as an order source

acceptance.when: Receiving tries to save a receipt
acceptance.then: The receipt is rejected and no stock movement is written

acceptance.given: An order is open for 10 units
acceptance.then: The order becomes Partially received with 4 units still open

acceptance.given: An invoice states a higher price than the order
acceptance.then: The invoice is Held and payment is blocked with the price difference named
The invoice is Verified, payment is scheduled and an audit entry is written

exceptions.expected: The request returns to the requester with the reason; no order can reference it.
Submission is blocked, the missing fields are named, and the draft is kept.
The request is routed to the next approver and stays Pending until a decision is made.

exceptions.scenario: Quantity received differs from the order
exceptions.expected: Accepted and rejected quantities are recorded; the order stays Partially received.
The invoice is Held, payment is blocked, and the mismatched field is named.
The second invoice is rejected against the existing invoice reference; payment is not repeated.

erp.note: Supplier, item and employee records exist before any transaction. An order cannot reference a supplier that is not master data.
Request, order, receipt, invoice and payment are documents with their own status and history.
Approval authority, receiving and payment are separate roles, not one administrator account.
The approval path depends on amount and role, and the decision is recorded with a reason.
The purchase order is the commitment between the approved request and the supplier.
A goods receipt changes stock; receiving the same order twice would corrupt the quantity.
The verified invoice becomes a payable; payment closes the loop and posts to the ledger.
Every state change keeps actor, time and previous state so the payment can be explained later.
Order, receipt and invoice must agree before money leaves the company.

in: One company, one warehouse and one currency.
Purchase request through payment, including approval and invoice verification.
Manual supplier selection and manual payment scheduling.
Audit trail for every state change.
out: Tax engine, e-invoicing and statutory reporting.
Supplier portal, contract management and budgeting.
limits: Northline Industrial Supply is fictional. The problems are illustrative, not field research.
The rules are written for this scenario, not as universal ERP rules.
No ERP product was configured and no supplier was contacted.
No measured outcome, time saving or cost reduction is claimed.
